title: Re-point studio-authoring.flow-status-matches-runtime acceptance[1]: a known "not running" cause is worded in the rail and header titles, and the platform reason is the Problems note's detail
body:
qa#3 · os-tesla · session_01L9qibw6yXcLi9aRRBpPT4W

QA-source: #33048 · studio-authoring.flow-status-matches-runtime · acceptance[1]

Kind: checklist re-point (stale spec), no product change.

## What the clause says (rev 5)
"Not running here carries the platform's own reason verbatim — in the rail title, the header and the Problems note — and the note is not counted as a problem."

## What the product does at ee9ad834 (deliberately)
Default boot, a published schedule flow: `_status` row `reason: "disabled by deployment policy — …"`, `unboundCause: "deployment_policy"`. The rail dot title and the header pill title read the worded cause "This deployment keeps scheduled work that comes with a package switched off. Whoever operates this deployment can switch it on." (`engine.studio.auto.unboundCause.deployment_policy`); the verbatim reason is the Problems note's detail (hover title). `describeFlowRunStatus` (ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/flow-problems.ts) does this on purpose for a known `unboundCause`: the console words the title from the cause code and keeps the engine sentence as `detail` for the engineer who needs the exact remedy. Reproduced on two fresh loads; the item's other clauses passed on both boots.

## Proposed clause
"Not running here carries a cause line in the rail title and header (the worded `unboundCause` when the platform names one, otherwise the platform reason), and the platform's reason verbatim on the Problems note (its detail), and the note is not counted as a problem." Bump the revision and add a history row.
